page: Microsoft Azure D192ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, delivering 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance bundles 11339 GB of local disk capacity, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance and memory throughput. The server achieves a top-tier rating in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores, driven by its massive core count and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 13906.45 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 268.41 GB/sec. Database and caching operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a top-tier Redis SET performance of 250.73 million operations per second and strong PassMark database operation scores.

While multi-threaded capabilities and prompt processing for large language models are highly competitive, single-core performance presents a relative tradeoff, scoring in the average tier for stress-ng single-core tests. Similarly, text generation speeds for smaller LLM models fall into the lower percentiles, whereas larger 70B model prompt processing remains in the top tier. Given the high resource density and massive local storage capacity, this server offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput static web serving, multi-threaded data decompression, and enterprise-grade general-purpose workloads.
